claims.text: The diagnosis is clinical, from history and examination.
claims.quote: Diagnosis is based on history and physical examination.

claims.text: Electrolytes for moderately or severely ill children and for those needing IV fluids, looking for hypernatremia, hypokalemia, metabolic acidosis or alkalosis.
claims.quote: Laboratory testing is usually reserved for moderately or severely ill children, in whom electrolyte disturbances (eg, hypernatremia , hypokalemia , metabolic acidosis , metabolic alkalosis ) are more common, and for children who need IV fluid therapy.

claims.text: Other lab findings: hemoconcentration, raised BUN and high urine specific gravity.
claims.quote: Other laboratory abnormalities in dehydration include relative polycythemia resulting from hemoconcentration, elevated blood urea nitrogen, and increased urine specific gravity.
If dehydration is suspected, or vomiting has been prolonged, serum electrolytes should be measured.
